title: Caracteristiques d' activité et de stabilité des vaccines antivarioliques utilisés dans les programmes d' éradication de la variole en Afrique de l' ouest et du centre-ouest / par A. Bernstein et M.Z. Bierly

sections.title: Page 1

summary.text: The first page of a 1972 WHO report in French on the potency and stability of smallpox vaccines used in the eradication programme in West and Central-West Africa, with a partly garbled OCR title. It credits the near-eradication of smallpox in the region to careful surveillance, effective vaccination and a heat-stable vaccine. It introduces the laboratory titrations and field tests reported, along with standard WHO distribution notices.

summary.text: Reports titration results for the reference vaccine and production lots for jet injector and bifurcated needle use, showing most lots met potency standards. It begins describing how the source of embryonated eggs, embryo age and inoculum volume affect titration on the chorioallantoic membrane. The OCR text contains garbled units and symbols.

sections.title: Page 4

summary.text: Reports that major reaction rates were similar across 18 vaccinated groups and changed little with dilution except at 1:100, suggesting current potency standards exceed what is needed. It compares titrations on embryonated eggs and cell culture and notes the virus strains behind different reference vaccines.

sections.title: Page 5

summary.text: Describes stability studies of freeze-dried Dryvax vaccine stored at various temperatures, showing only modest titre loss after months at 25°C or 37°C. It reports long-term stability at 2–8°C and that reconstituted vaccine lost potency faster with a diluent containing phenol.
